Here, for m, n : N.A1, N.D8 m n (defined as N.D7 n m) means that there exist functions σ, σ' : (k : N.A1) → N.A3 k and an element x : X such that σ k = σ' k for all k ≠ m, and N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x. The relation Relation.TransGen N.D8 m n means that there is a chain m = c_0, c_1, ..., c_k = n of length k ≥ 1 (at least one step; zero steps do not count) with N.D8 c_i c_{i+1} for every step. None of these definitions asserts or proves that the propositions hold for any N.

1. D11 N : Prop is the proposition that both: (a) N.A1 is nonempty (has at least one element), and (b) for all m, n : N.A1, Relation.TransGen N.D8 m n holds (there is a chain of at least one N.D8-step from m to n). Because m and n are not restricted to be distinct and Relation.TransGen requires at least one step, D11 N also requires every element m : N.A1 to have a nonempty N.D8-chain back to itself (for example, if N.A1 has a single element m, D11 N still requires N.D8 m m to hold). It places no conditions on N.a4 or N.a6.

2. D12 N : Prop is the proposition that for all m, n : N.A1, if m ≠ n, then it is not the case that both Relation.TransGen N.D8 m n and Relation.TransGen N.D8 n m hold. That is, no two distinct elements of N.A1 can each reach the other via a chain of at least one N.D8-step (equivalently, there is no directed N.D8-cycle containing two or more distinct elements). Because of the hypothesis m ≠ n, D12 N does not forbid self-loops N.D8 m m (cycles staying at a single element m), nor does it require N.A1 to be nonempty. It places no conditions on N.a4 or N.a6.

3. d13 N : ℕ is defined as Fintype.card N.A1, the cardinality (number of elements) of the finite type N.A1 (using the Fintype instance N.a2).

divergences.description: In [P-D52b] and [P-HW], conscious recurrent systems (characterized quantitatively by IIT's ϕ > 0, including arbitrarily high ϕ) and strictly feed-forward systems (Φ = 0) are mutually exclusive. Although the author explicitly disclaims equivalence to ϕ > 0, replacing it with the qualitative strong-feedback stand-in D11 while allowing self-loops in D12 makes the two predicates non-disjoint: any single-unit system with a self-loop (such as d15 in the context) satisfies both D11 and D12.

Because S1 allows each unit n : N.A1 to have an arbitrary (even infinite) state space N.A3 n and arbitrary update function N.a5 n, d13 counts units without constraining per-unit capacity, whereas 'neurons' in [P-D54] implicitly represent simple/bounded computational units. Likewise, omitting the elementary-component (flip-flop) requirement of [P-HW]—which the author explicitly disclaims for D12—means any finite-state system trivially satisfies D12 when collapsed into a single unit.

judgement.summary: All three definitions formally match the author's specific claims: D11 captures nonempty strong feedback, D12 is (by finiteness of N.A1) mathematically equivalent to the existence of a hierarchical ordering where earlier units transition independently of later ones while permitting self-loops, and d13 is the unit count. The only divergences relative to the source passages are minor caveats stemming from the model's abstractions—chiefly the overlap of D11 and D12 on single-unit self-looping systems and the unconstrained state spaces of individual units compared with biological/artificial neurons or flip-flops.
